note: A static practice-question bank that works offline. The product does not predict exact interview questions; it provides realistic practice to reduce uncertainty, not answers to memorize.
designNote: The support profile is not a diagnosis. It records support preferences that the user chooses, can inspect, edit, disable, or delete at any time.

profileQuestions.label: Communication
profileQuestions.question: When you receive an unexpected question, what usually helps?

options.text: Have the question broken into smaller parts

profileQuestions.label: Information format
profileQuestions.question: For complex instructions, which format works best for you?

profileQuestions.label: Work style
profileQuestions.question: When do you usually work at your best?

supportActions.label: Need a moment
supportActions.description: Ask for a brief pause to organize your thoughts instead of rushing an incomplete answer.

supportActions.label: Clarify the focus
supportActions.description: Ask which aspect matters most when a question could be interpreted in several ways.

supportActions.label: Break it down
supportActions.description: Split a multi-part question into smaller pieces and answer them one at a time.

questions.text: An API returns a 500 error. How would you trace the cause?
parts: What information would you check first?
How would you narrow down possible causes?
How would you confirm the fix works?

questions.text: You receive code-review feedback that you disagree with. What would you do?
parts: How would you understand the reviewer’s concern?
How would you explain your reasoning?
What would you do if you still disagreed?

questions.text: A React application is growing. How would you reorganize its structure?
parts: How would you decide where to split the code?
How would you manage shared code?
How would you reduce unnecessary coupling?
focusOptions: A relevant example from your experience

questions.text: Tell me about a difficult technical problem you solved.
parts: What was the context and the problem?
What steps did you take?
What was the outcome?
What did you learn?

questions.text: Tell me about a time you balanced competing priorities while maintaining stakeholder alignment.
parts: Which priorities were in conflict?
How did you decide what mattered most?
How did you communicate the decision?
What happened afterward?
focusOptions: The outcome and what you learned

questions.text: Tell me a little about yourself.
parts: What are you doing now?
What brought you to this point?
Why are you interested in this role?

questions.text: If a teammate disagreed with your implementation, how would you handle it?
parts: How would you understand their concern?
How would you explain your evidence?
How would you resolve the disagreement?
focusOptions: How you preserve the working relationship
How you support a technical decision

questions.text: You realize you will miss a deadline. What would you do?
parts: When did you notice the risk?
Who would you tell, and how?
What options would you propose?
focusOptions: How early and clearly you communicate risk

questions.text: You are given a task with unclear requirements. Where would you start?
parts: How would you identify what is unclear?
Who would you ask, and what would you ask?
When would you begin implementation?
focusOptions: How you avoid working in the wrong direction

questions.text: What would you hope to achieve in your first 90 days in this role?
parts: What would you learn first?
What would you try to contribute early?
How would you know you were making progress?

questions.text: Why did you choose this role rather than a different one?
parts: What about the work interests you?
What could you contribute to the role?
focusOptions: How your capabilities relate to the role

questions.text: If your preferred working conditions were not immediately available, what alternative would you propose, and why?
parts: Which condition matters most to you?
What alternative would you suggest?
How would you evaluate whether it works?
